items.followUp: State two differences between TEM and SEM.

rubric.why: TEM reveals internal structures by transmitting electrons through a thin specimen.
rubric.description: Identifies how TEM examines the specimen or what it reveals.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that electrons pass through a thin specimen to show its internal structure.

rubric.why: SEM scans the specimen's surface and produces a three-dimensional image.
rubric.description: Identifies how SEM examines the specimen or the image it produces.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that SEM scans the surface or produces a 3D image.

modelAnswer: TEM passes electrons through a very thin specimen to show its internal structures.
SEM scans the specimen’s surface and produces a three-dimensional image.

items.followUp: How did Antonie van Leeuwenhoek contribute to the discovery of cells?

rubric.why: Hooke examined a thin slice of cork using a microscope.
rubric.description: States what Hooke examined and/or the instrument he used.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning cork and its examination with a microscope.

rubric.why: He saw small compartments and named them cells.
rubric.description: States what Hooke observed or how the term cells arose.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that the small compartments he observed were called cells.

modelAnswer: Robert Hooke examined a thin slice of cork with a microscope.
He saw tiny box-like compartments and named them cells.

items.followUp: Write down two characteristics of kingdom Fungi.

rubric.why: Protists are eukaryotic; many are unicellular, live in water or moist places, and may be autotrophic or heterotrophic.
rubric.description: Gives one valid characteristic of kingdom Protista.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for any one correct characteristic.

rubric.why: Protists are eukaryotic; many are unicellular, live in water or moist places, and may be autotrophic or heterotrophic.
rubric.description: Gives a second valid characteristic of kingdom Protista.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a second correct characteristic.

modelAnswer: Kingdom Protista consists of eukaryotic organisms; most are unicellular.
Protists may be autotrophic or heterotrophic.

items.followUp: What is crossing over, and during which stage of meiosis does it occur?

rubric.why: Synapsis is the pairing of homologous chromosomes.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying it as the pairing of homologous chromosomes.

rubric.why: Synapsis occurs during prophase I of meiosis, specifically in zygotene.
rubric.description: Identifies where or when synapsis occurs.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating prophase I or zygotene.

modelAnswer: Synapsis is the pairing of homologous chromosomes.
It occurs during prophase I of meiosis, specifically in the zygotene stage.

items.followUp: Briefly explain how cytokinesis occurs in an animal cell.

rubric.why: In plant cells, a cell plate forms in the middle of the cell.
rubric.description: States where the cell plate forms during plant cytokinesis.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the formation of a cell plate at the centre of the cell.

rubric.why: The cell plate grows outward and joins the existing cell membrane, forming a new cell wall between the daughter cells.
rubric.description: Explains how the cell plate develops to separate the daughter cells.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it extends outward and forms or joins to make the dividing wall.

modelAnswer: A cell plate forms in the middle of the plant cell.
It grows outward until it joins the cell membrane, forming a new cell wall between the daughter cells.

items.followUp: Differentiate between a somatic cell and a gamete.

rubric.why: Somatic cells are body cells and are generally diploid; they are produced by mitosis.
rubric.description: Gives a valid characteristic of a somatic cell.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying somatic cells as body cells or stating their diploid nature or mitotic production.

rubric.why: Germ-line cells occur in reproductive organs and give rise to gametes through meiosis.
rubric.description: Gives a valid characteristic of a germ-line cell.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking germ-line cells to gamete production, reproductive organs, or meiosis.

modelAnswer: Somatic cells are body cells, generally diploid, and are produced by mitosis.
Germ-line cells occur in reproductive organs and produce gametes by meiosis.

items.followUp: Name two products made using anaerobic respiration by microorganisms.

rubric.why: Yeast fermentation is used in bread-making and in producing alcohol such as ethanol.
rubric.description: Names one use of fermentation involving yeast.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a valid use such as bread-making or alcohol production.

rubric.why: Bacterial fermentation is used to make products such as yogurt and cheese.
rubric.description: Names another valid use of fermentation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a second valid use, such as making yogurt or cheese.

modelAnswer: Fermentation by yeast is used in making bread and producing alcohol such as ethanol.
Bacterial fermentation is used in making yogurt and cheese.

items.followUp: What is meant by a biological catalyst, and how does it affect a reaction?

rubric.why: Enzymes are biological catalysts produced by living cells.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that enzymes are biological catalysts or are catalysts made by living organisms.

rubric.why: Enzymes speed up biochemical reactions without being consumed in the process.
rubric.description: Explains the catalytic action of enzymes.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that enzymes increase reaction rate or are not consumed.

modelAnswer: Enzymes are called biocatalysts because they are biological catalysts produced by living cells.
They speed up biochemical reactions without being consumed in the process.
